answer.evidence: The tile is a 48x32 sand surface seen from above. Rows 0-7 are the terrace lip (L about 178). A dark broken line at rows 9-11 marks the lip edge, and the lighter ramp surface (L about 199-210) runs from row 12 to row 31. A faint darker line at row 24 and a gentle lightening toward the bottom suggest the slope. Narrow dark strips at the left and right edges (about 2-3 px wide, from row 7 down) are the cut walls seen edge-on. There is no vertical south face of 3 or more rows, so the whole tile reads as a flat top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a sand ramp built from about 9 colours in total. It has a light top band, a mid-tan body and a few darker horizontal strokes, with only sparse speckle. The picture shows large areas of one flat tan, and the measured near-flat coverage is 20% against 0% for both references. Visible tones per tile (5) are above the grass reference (3) but below the paving reference (7), and raw colours per tile (6) are far below the grass reference (26). The grass reference reads as richer because it carries tufts and several greens. The sand has no grain, no per-pixel clumps and no pebbles, so the sand does not read as a textured surface. The 4-step ramp (highlight, light, mid, edge) is shallower than the 5-6 steps Beodeul uses. The outline is a tinted brown, with 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so it is not a sticker look. The slope direction also reads weakly, as a lit top lip over a flat body with no visible rise or descent.
